title: Not a Matter for the Council

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager mocked a neighbor's singing at the fire, and the neighbor asks the council for help: hear both, or suggest they talk.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the fire last night, (subject) said loudly that (friend)'s singing sounded like a seabird with a cold. People laughed. (friend) didn't. Today (friend) has asked the council to do something about it.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The council listens and says that rudeness isn't against any rule, and it won't punish it. But one elder, (elder), adds, plainly, that it was unkind, and that (subject) knows it. (subject) shifts in (subject.his/her) seat. The council also says that (friend) may sit wherever (friend.he/she) likes at the fire, and needn't sit anywhere near (subject). (friend) sits on the far side. (subject) notices, all evening.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The council suggests that (friend) tell (subject) directly how it felt. (friend) does, briefly: "You made people laugh at me. I won't sing near you again." (subject) begins to say it was only a joke, and stops. "...All right." Whether (friend) ever sings near (subject.him/her) again is entirely up to (friend). For now, (friend.he/she) doesn't. Sometimes (subject) hears (friend.him/her) singing on the far side of the village, and stays quiet.
